task.problem: All manifolds are connected and compact. Write dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Use genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives. For a smooth real (1,1) form theta, PSH(X,theta) means theta+dd^c u>=0. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C and equivalence means mutual order, including the canonical values at common poles. Extended products mean non-pluripolar Monge-Ampere products with smooth-background corrections. A big background admits a genuine strict current theta+dd^c u>=epsilon h for some Hermitian h and epsilon>0. BMP means v_+(h)<infinity, where v_+(h) and v_-(h) are the supremum and infimum of integral(h+dd^c u)^n over all bounded h-psh u. Positive lower mass means v_-(h)>0; it is distinct from BMP. Fix a Hermitian h on a manifold of dimension n>=2 and a finite nonzero positive non-pluripolar Borel measure nu, meaning it gives zero mass to every locally pluripolar Borel set. Do not assume nu has a density against smooth volume. Original S15 asks for intrinsic individual criteria distinguishing (A) some genuine h-psh u and a>0 with MA_ext_h(u)>=a nu, (B) an exact finite-mass equation MA_ext_h(u)=c nu with c>0 and sup u=0, and (C) MA_ext_h(u)=exp(lambda u)nu for a specified lambda>0, with a natural class and any normalization correctly stated. Exponential equations are not invariant under adding constants with their scalar fixed. Known background: v_-(h)>0 is equivalent to exact solvability for every finite non-pluripolar measure in the relative envelope class E_env(X,h,0). Here E_env consists of u preceq phi such that for each t>=1 some genuine h-psh v satisfies t^(-1)v+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u; unrestricted envelope equality is not its definition. At zero lower mass even absolutely continuous probability measures bounded below by a positive constant can have no positive scaled subsolution, although every smooth density is solvable. For individual density f dV, the bounded truncation constants define b_h(f)=lim_k c_h(min(f,k)), exactly characterize positive scaled subsolutions and attain the maximal coefficient. A maximal subsolution may have excess or infinite mass, so this does not alone answer (B). General nu has no canonical bounded truncation relative to smooth volume. Existing prescribed-reference measure theorems have model, lower-volume and genuine smaller-background hypotheses. Bounded concentration obstructions do not settle unbounded exponential solvability. No replacement threshold, measure construction or proof is supplied.
task.completionCriteria: Give a new intrinsic and non-tautological individual criterion for general non-pluripolar nu, with complete implications for scaled subsolutions, exact finite-mass normalized equations and exponential equations distinguished precisely. A new sufficient-condition theorem must cover a substantive measure singular with respect to smooth volume and address the stated zero-lower-mass or prescribed-type obstruction beyond the known positive-lower-mass universal theorem. Do not define the criterion merely as existence of the requested subsolution, silently insert bounded-density truncations, or infer an exact finite-mass product from an attained inequality. Verify compactness, domination, canonical representatives and indispensable primary sources; independently reconstruct the full proof and retain any unresolved assertions.

assignment:
For the proposed restricted sufficient-condition theorem, let X0 be any connected compact Hermitian m-fold with v_-(h0)=0, V0=integral h0^m, X=X0 x P1, N=m+1, H=h0+kappa and integral kappa=1. Use the unchanged original task operator and genuine products. On the projective line let G(x,y)=log(d_chord(x,y)^2)+1, with the usual chordal distance of diameter1. Let mu be a Borel probability for which the explicit actual kernel integral Q_mu(x)=integral G(x,y)dmu(y) is finite and continuous at every point. For M>0 put nu=M(h0^m/V0) tensor mu and c=N V0/M. These are hypotheses and definitions, not accepted conclusions.

Reconstruct the following unproved targets from this statement and independently retrieved primary material, or identify an exact gap. A: Prove the normalization of G, non-pluripolarity of mu and nu, nonclosedness and zero lower mass of H, and u=Q_mu-sup Q_mu as a genuine bounded continuous supremum-zero solution MA_ext_H(u)=c nu of actual finite mass N V0. Keep the basic existence implication for 0<a<=c separate from the additional maximal-coefficient assertion proposed in G, which must itself be independently proved. B: For EVERY specified lambda>0 construct a bounded continuous genuine curve solution w_lambda of kappa+ddc w_lambda=exp(lambda w_lambda)mu, integral exp(lambda w_lambda)dmu=1, and prove bounded curve uniqueness. No proof method or intermediate measure trace is supplied. C: Prove U_lambda=log(c)/lambda+w_lambda gives the actual scalar-one product exponential equation, retain sup U_lambda, give the correct coefficient after supremum normalization, and verify the genuine all-scale zero-reference stretching class directly. D: Prove uniform whole-family w_lambda -> Q_mu-integral Q_mu dmu with O(lambda) error, supremum-normalized convergence to u, and the separated critical-subsolution order characterization for all genuine curve critical subsolutions. E: Prove the criterion for any probability with mu(B_chord(x,r))<=C r^delta, delta>0, and verify the nonconstant weighted-circle probability (1+epsilon cos theta)dtheta/(2pi), 0<epsilon<1, is a substantive singular example with nonconstant potential on its support. The theorem is conditional on the stated factor hypothesis. The concrete named factor is a separate complete independent dependency, to be assessed in the combined full/final proof rather than supplied as a trusted note here. Do not claim original unrestricted S15 closure. A maximal scalar characterization is now a separate unproved target G under the same continuous-potential hypotheses.

F: Separately discard the finite continuous-potential hypothesis on mu and assume only that mu is a Borel probability charging no polar Borel set on P1. Independently prove that the actual same kernel integral Q_mu is a genuine possibly unbounded kappa-psh function with mean zero, and that (Q_mu-sup Q_mu) pulled back gives an exact finite-mass supremum-zero equation MA_ext_H(u)=c nu. Prove non-pluripolarity of this nu and uniqueness in the sector of pullbacks of genuine kappa-psh curve potentials. Prove, in this sector, bounded solution existence if and only if Q_mu is bounded, and continuous solution existence if and only if Q_mu is continuous. Preserve all genuine pole values. Do not infer bounded exponential existence or zero-reference stretching membership for arbitrary unbounded Q from this additional target. This statement supplies no proof method or author argument.

G: Under the finite continuous-potential criterion, independently prove that the constructed bounded product exponential solution U_lambda is greatest among ALL genuine H-psh exponential subsolutions, including competitors with additional poles or excess or infinite mass. Prove bounded product solution uniqueness. Prove that c=NV0/M is the attained supremum of a>=0 such that MA_ext_H(v)>=a nu over every genuine H-psh v, and that the same value is attained in the bounded ordinary type and the exact zero-reference stretching class. This is a measure threshold without smooth-volume density truncations. Do not claim unbounded exponential solution uniqueness or critical-potential uniqueness outside the separated sector. No author proof or method for these targets is supplied. Verify every exact external hypothesis freshly; no BMP or Lp volume-density existence premise is granted for the singular measure.
